products.product_id: Unique product identifier (primary key); format P### (e.g., P001)
products.product_name: Human-readable product name; 20 unique products across all categories
products.category: Product classification; 5 distinct categories (Electronics, Apparel, Sport, Home & Kitchen, Sports)
products.standard_price: List price for product; ranges $12.99–$999.99, mean $259.24

sales_data.transaction_id: Unique transaction identifier; format TXN##### or RET##### (returns); 8 nulls (4.3%), 166 unique values
sales_data.transaction_date: Date of transaction; mixed formats (MM/DD/YYYY and YYYY-MM-DD); 116 unique dates spanning Jan–Mar 2024
sales_data.store_id: Foreign key to stores table; 5 nulls (2.69%), 10 unique store references (S01–S10)
sales_data.product_id: Foreign key to products table; 20 unique products, no nulls
sales_data.product_name: Denormalized product name from products table; 20 unique values
sales_data.category: Denormalized product category; 21 unique values (note: 1 extra vs products.category, likely data quality issue)
sales_data.quantity: Units sold per transaction; range -4 to +8 (negative = returns/refunds), mean 3.94
sales_data.unit_price: Price per unit at time of sale; range $0.01–$9,999.99, mean $356.27 (high variance suggests data quality issues)
sales_data.total_amount: Transaction total (quantity × unit_price); range -$1,230.56 to $9,999.99, mean $1,215.24 (negative = refunds)
sales_data.customer_segment: Customer classification; 16 unique segments (Loyal, Premium, etc.)
sales_data.payment_method: Payment type; 4 unique methods (Apple Pay, PayPal, etc.)

stores.store_id: Unique store identifier (primary key); format S## (S01–S10)
stores.region: Geographic region; 4 unique regions (Northeast, Southeast, etc.)

join_keys.notes: Perfect cardinality match (20 unique products in both); no nulls in sales_data.product_id; enables enrichment with standard_price
Cardinality match (10 unique stores); 5 nulls (2.69%) in sales_data.store_id require handling; enables enrichment with store location/region

quality_notes: CRITICAL: transaction_id has 8 nulls (4.3%) — records lack unique transaction identifiers; impacts auditability and deduplication
CRITICAL: store_id has 5 nulls (2.69%) — orphaned transactions cannot be attributed to stores; join will drop these records
CRITICAL: transaction_date format inconsistency — mixed MM/DD/YYYY and YYYY-MM-DD formats; requires standardization before parsing
CRITICAL: category cardinality mismatch — sales_data has 21 unique categories vs products has 5; suggests data quality issue (typos, case sensitivity, or extra values)
HIGH: Negative quantities (-4 to -1) and negative total_amounts indicate returns/refunds; consider separate handling or flag in fact table
HIGH: unit_price variance is extreme ($0.01–$9,999.99, mean $356.27); outliers at $9,999.99 suggest data entry errors or test records
MEDIUM: Denormalization in sales_data — product_name and category duplicated from products table; violates normalization; consider removing in bronze/silver layer
MEDIUM: customer_segment has 16 unique values but no null check; verify against master customer dimension if one exists
MEDIUM: payment_method has only 4 unique values; low cardinality suggests limited payment options or data aggregation
LOW: products.standard_price has 19 unique values for 20 products (1 duplicate price); minor data quality note
